answer: A rendering service making dune landscapes, jade ornaments and lotus animations should sell CPU shares, not grant each agent an equal scheduling lane. Track each purchased share in one ledger and let its owner divide it among queues without increasing the total. Schedule CPU time in proportion to those shares, with no minimum allocation per identity. Splitting a ten-share account into ten aliases then leaves its total service entitlement unchanged. This blocks queue multiplication as a Sybil advantage, while wealthy customers can still buy more capacity.
